change_summary: New quant/news_replay.py module with _T1_NEGATIVE_KEYWORDS classifier, get_news_for_date(), apply_news_gate(). BacktestEngine gained replay_news parameter and --replay-news CLI flag. news_attribution bucket added to result (parallel to llm_attribution). known_biases.news_veto_unreplayed.archive_replay_enabled now reflects replay_news state.

delta_metrics.note: Off-mode: bit-identical to before_metrics (pure passthrough). On-mode: zero vetoes across 6 signals on 13 covered days 闂?news_veto bias is NEGLIGIBLE for this window. The optimistic bias from un-replayed news veto is smaller than feared: quant signals and T1-negative news are anti-correlated (bullish quant signal rarely coincides with bearish T1 news).

hypothesis: Building news_replay.py (parallel to llm_replay.py) to apply T1-negative news veto in backtester --replay-news mode closes the 闂?.1 news-veto parity gap for covered dates. Off-mode metrics must be identical to baseline; on-mode measures the actual veto impact.
notes: Key insight: 0 vetoes out of 6 signals on 13 covered days. This is expected 闂?if a ticker has T1-negative news (earnings miss, guidance cut), the quant signal engine would likely NOT generate a bullish trend/breakout signal for it on that day (stock would be down, trend broken). The two filters are anti-correlated. This means the 'news veto bias' label overstates the actual gap 闂?the bias exists in theory but may be near-zero in practice for pure quant signals. In 217 pytest tests pass. Establish true baseline EV score: 0.4875 (updated from 0.4954, which was stale from before market data refresh).
